utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everybody. If I may, I should like to ask for a correction. I went through yesterday's transcript, and I noticed that towards the end, on page 120, page 120, in line 22, it says, wrongly, that Mr. Mario Cerkez was on the videotape that was shown us yesterday. This was obviously an error, and it should read "Mr. Dario Kordic". That is the only correction that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. That will be noted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Sahinovic, shall we go on with our conversation with our questions yesterday. You said yesterday that you had never heard about Mr. Dario Kordic before he addressed you on the 24th February, '92. Busovaca is not far from Novi Travnik, about 30 kilometres or something, I believe. It's close, it's not far. The whole Lasva Valley is rather small, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And although this whole area is very small, you never heard about Mr. Kordic before that date, that is, 24 February, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move on to something else. The shipment document, that is the document that was adduced by the Prosecution as Exhibit Number 78A and B. You did say something yesterday about that, but could you tell us, had you been going to the -- were you going to the factory, to the plant, during that period? On the 22nd of April, which is indicated on the document, were you at the factory then?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Sahinovic, as the president of the union, you knew about everything that was going on there, including those armaments shipments?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mostly through the Workers' Council and the manager and his associates.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: We were also informed in that way that on the 22nd of April, '92, there were also negotiations that took place between the SDA and HDZ precisely about these weapons, or whatever they were called, indicated in the document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You have no knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In this receipt that was shown us yesterday, you said that a stamp was of the Secretariat for National Defence of the municipality of Busovaca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From the text, when I read the seal, yes, I recognised it as the one of the Territorial Defence of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You also recognised and there is an indicated signature of Mr. Dario Kordic on that receipt?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: It is, therefore, evident that that person who put the stamp wanted it to be known that he had taken over what was indicated in that receipt?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But it transpires from this document that the person who signed it and who put the stamp there, that he had taken over?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I do not know if that is the signature of Mr. Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But we do agree that his name is on that receipt, who took over what it says there?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, as the union president, you say that you're acquainted with the armaments shipments and so forth. I should now like to ask you about some sizeable amounts of quantities of armaments and materiel, not only weapons, which left Bratstvo on the basis of an agreement between the SDA and the HDZ. Within that context, I should like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You do know?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know, but I do not know what the quantities were, and the Territorial Defence headquarters of Travnik took over a certain quantity. Likewise, the headquarters in Vitez and in Novi Travnik. But what quantities were they, I would not be able to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: That was what I was about to ask you. So we agree that those shipments of weapons and materiel which were at Bratstvo were distributed between one and the other party to the headquarters of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were allotted certain quantities of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I should like to ask you specifically, do you know Mr. Osman Cengic, according to these agreements that I mentioned between the HDZ and the SDA about the distribution of the weapons, took over a large quantity of these weapons and materiel for Sarajevo so that this whole convoy went through the Lasva Valley to Visoko, escorted by the civilian police from Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You know nothing about that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: A very large quantity. They are talking about 21 trucks. You know nothing about that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You know nothing about it?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, these weapons which were distributed on the basis of the agreement, it made part of the final balance about the distribution of weapons, about the division of weapons between the SDA and the HDZ; do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You have no information?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When you spoke about events after November, 1992, you said there were victims in Novi Travnik after that month; after, that is, 11 November, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that those casualties -- those victims of crimes in Novi Travnik, there were also Croats after November, '92?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Sahinovic, you made your statement, and, it says here, on the 5th of March and 8th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And the interpreter was Emina Kaknjo?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Would the usher please show the statement to the witness? We also have copies for the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit is marked D3/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I wish to draw your attention to item 15 of the statement. And 15 on the fifth page, Mr. Sahinovic, the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you're referring to what happened as of November, '92. You said that the victims of those crimes included also some Croats. The second sentence from the top -- rather the first one in the first line. Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (No audible response)

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Sahinovic, did you find that sentence to which I wish to draw your attention in the first line on that page? On the fifth one, it begins with the word "maju", which means "among", and relates to the period after November, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you agree that that is what you stated, that during the events after November, '92, there were also some Croats?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but this is a period which refers to the arrival of Herzegovinians in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, but the paragraph begins with the words "From November, '92"?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you do agree that -- you agree, in other words, that Croats were also victims of crimes which happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I said, and I was very clear, it was after Herzegovinians arrived in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure that -- I also meant Croat victims. Do we agree about Croat victims? Do we agree about that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: A while ago -- no, I mean when we discussed that receipt, I think I was also warned that there was an error in the transcript. They said that it was the headquarters of the Territorial Defence of Busovaca, and it should be Secretariat for National Defence of Busovaca. You remember that stamp that we discussed a little while ago? So will you please correct that? It was the seal of the Secretariat for National Defence of the municipality of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Sahinovic, I have to ask you a few things which I believe are also important. As a soldier, that action, that fighting that went on in the village of Lazine in the summer of '93, it was a military operation, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Likewise, the fighting that went on at Isakovici in February '93, it was also a military operation?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but civilians, and the Isakovici was a place which was inhabited by civilians, Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm asking you if it was a military operation. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but the defence line went through the village of Isakovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: That was what I wanted to ask you. It was a military operation. Thank you. Tell us, please, you are saying, if I understood you properly, that as of November '92, you became the head of the security service of the 308th Brigade of the B and H army?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, municipal headquarters of the Territorial Defence. I was appointed deputy commander for security matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, my mistake.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The brigade did not exist yet, and when the brigade was formed, then another man was appointed deputy commander for security matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I understand. I'm asking about when you were invited there, you were invited to report to that duty from the office you occupied before?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And you were told that you would be involved in counterintelligence?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, that I would be deputy commander of Refik Lendo for security matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You were not told what your responsibilities would be?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not know whether you understand what deputy assistant commander for security in the municipality headquarters in the headquarters of the Territorial Defence in the municipality of Busovaca means.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I am asking you if you were told that you would be involved in counterintelligence against the enemy.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the service, as such, encompasses such duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, who were enemies at the time?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, we were oriented towards the Chetniks only; however, when the Croatian Defence Council attacked Novi Travnik, we also came to think that they were our enemies too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So we agree that in November '92, the enemy, to your mind, were both Chetniks and the Croats of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After those victims?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. We are talking about November of '92?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, when we say Chetniks, just for the sake of clarification, you mean Serb forces, in the broad sense?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In those duties you discharged, you knew what was happening throughout that area which was under you, and later on, of the 308th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When the 308th Mountain Brigade was appointed, the deputy commander was then responsible for the security, and I was a commander of the municipal headquarters, so that my zone of responsibility extended in the direction of Novi Travnik to Rostovo, and I was involved with the separation of crime, since this was the only way which linked up Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, but tell us, please, since this is your area, Sebesici, Rostovo, that part, I mean -- and you say that is your part?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So could you please tell us, if you know, who was it that in January manned the checkpoint at Ravno Rostovo?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At Ravno Rostovo? Will you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Early '91 (sic), January, February.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no, I can't -- I don't remember, really, whether it was the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I meant the forces: Whose forces?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At Rostovo, if you want me to be very specific, we had a camp, the 308th Mountain Brigade was preparing their units for Bugojno, where we were manning the line towards Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: No, but was this checkpoint manned by the forces of the 308th Mounted Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking you: Who was it that manned that checkpoint? I'm sorry, I'm being warned about an error. We are talking about this checkpoint at Ravno Rostovo, I think I was asking you about '93, and it says here January, February, '91. So will you please rectify this: We are talking about January, February, of '93.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, since this was the zone of Bugojno, I think it was the civilian police at the time, civilian police from Bugojno, and the 308th Brigade, the Territorial Defence, never had a checkpoint there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, please, in the municipality of Novi Travnik, according to the information that we have, there were also Mujahedin units active there, and as the head -- or rather as the man who was responsible for those things that you said, you had information about the Mujahedin in that area?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Are you telling the Court that about the Mujahedin in the municipality of Novi Travnik, you know nothing?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't. Nor do I have any information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But as the man who was responsible for counterintelligence there?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. What I then need to ask you, in that same -- at that same checkpoint at Ravno Rostovo, during that period of time that we are talking about, that is, early 1993, Mujahedin looted an HVO convoy; the Mujahedin, who were manning that checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You know nothing about that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you have information about some other convoys who went that way?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do about convoys which went through Opara.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know about a convoy which went to Usvara or rather Trenica and Tuzla, a joint convoy?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I escorted that convoy to the Intrain zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Were there any problems regarding that convoy?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: To the man who was heading that convoy, I personally advised not to go through Novi Travnik, controlled by the HVO, for the sake of their safety. However, the man who was leading that convoy --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Excuse me, when I meant "problems," I did not mean the HVO, but the part that was controlled by you, or rather by the army of the BHA.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That convoy spent the night in Pavlovica, mostly in inhabited areas among the Muslims. And I can affirm that the Muslims welcomed over them lunch and dinner, what they had, and there were no problems at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: There were no incidents, there was no looting in the area which was under your control?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not of that convoy, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, since we're talking about Opara, if I understood you properly, you were born somewhere around Opara, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the neighbourhood community of Zagrlje, but that is that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In Opara there is an elementary school, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In Opara, on the grounds of the elementary school, in summer of 1993, prisoners were kept; it served as a camp?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Are you telling the Court that in that school, that school did not house a detention camp?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The detention camp did not exist in Opara, and I do affirm that positively.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: No, in the school.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the school, there was only a provisional detention unit for soldiers of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina detained for crimes and some other offences and who were then taken into custody there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In the building of the elementary school?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But I'm talking about 25 Croats who were detained in Opara. I do not mean only the soldiers of the BH army. Were those people detained in the elementary school, the Croats?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All those who happened to --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you, were the Croats detained there?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Opara, as far as I can remember, they were from Trenica. I cannot remember how many, but they must have been in that hall in the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm talking about 25 people. So there were also Croats detained in the elementary school in Opara?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the same area where the members of the BH army were detained, and that room is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, this is becoming unclear and confused. Now, are you putting to the witness that 25 Croats were detained in Opara? Is that the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I think the witness has just answered that question. That was indeed my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you what your question was. It's not at all clear to those listening. Now, let me ask the witness this: What is suggested is that there were 25 Croats detained in Opara. Is that right, or not?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And whereabouts were they detained?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the gym, in the school building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And when was it that they were detained, and for how long?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: During the conflict between the BH army and the HVO. I cannot tell you the exact date, but in view of the fact that the local people who stayed behind in Trenica, which is some way from Opara -- actually the distance is about ten kilometres -- for security reasons, these people were transferred to Opara.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Sahinovic, were you personally in command of the military police that was in Opara and connected to the school that we are referring to?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you personally interrogate the detainees, the Croats who were detained there?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not the ones in Trenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: However, the Croatian soldiers who were held prisoner in Opara?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Was it part of your duty to be in charge of this facility, whatever you like to call it, the school, during the time when people were detained there?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. There was a senior officer, as this was treated as a barracks, so the senior officer in the hierarchy was always in charge. He was the person responsible for the facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. But when you came, in view of your position, you were superior to that local commander?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you have a command responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, please, perhaps just two or three questions about Novi Travnik. Were you in the town of Novi Travnik in the summer of 1993, in August, 1993? August, 1993, were you in the town? That is, in the part under the control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly now, since I was mostly engaged in the area of Opara, as I have already said. But as necessary, I was in town too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I should like to ask you a few questions, but if you weren't there, there is no point in tiring Their Honours. That is why I'm asking you this question: Were you in the town of Novi Travnik in August 1993?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm afraid I cannot tell you with precision at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Perhaps, through the questions I will put to you, that will help to refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The part of the town that was held by the HVO was left without water in August 1993 because the water supply was cut off. That is what I wanted to ask you. Do you know that? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not aware about the water, but as far as I know, the water coming from Opara, going through the supply system, passes through the lower part of the city, which was under the control of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, but I was thinking of the water supply system coming through the other part of the city. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The water supply comes from Opara. The water supply for the town of Novi Travnik comes from Opara.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But my question is about the water supply system passing through the part of the town controlled by the BH army and running towards the HVO part of the town. Do you know that that water supply system was closed in '93?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: May I explain to Their Honours, the question is wrong. The supply system goes from Opara, passes through the HVO-controlled part of the city, and then reaches the part of the town that was under the control of the BH army, and not vice versa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you're talking only about one water supply system?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is the main water supply system for Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So are you saying there's no water supply system coming from the part under the BH army control going towards the HVO-controlled part of the town? That's what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, the other water supply system that exists is used exclusively for the Bratstvo factory, from the moment the water supply started running to Novi Travnik from Opara.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, but again, we do not seem to understand one another. So there's one part of the water supply going from the part of the town controlled by the BH army into the HVO part controlled area of town?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, there was no such water supply system.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Sahinovic, the Croatian Defence Council and the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, they were two components of the unified armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, were they not?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know which period you are referring to, but I do know that until 1992, when I placed myself at the disposal of the Territorial Defence, there was a joint command which was composed of both Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But those were the beginnings, this was just after the Serbs attacked in April '92, that's the period you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there was a joint command, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But my question has to do with '92, '93, and the whole period up to the Washington Agreement.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know how it is defined by law, but I know that there was no joint command after the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: My question was, do you agree with me that the Croatian Defence Council and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were components of the unified armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question because they were confronted parties. How can they be joint forces when they were in conflict with one another?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpreted) Your Honours, we should like to tender several documents, and one of them could be shown to the witness. The first exhibit is a decree with the force of law adopted by the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 2nd of February, 1992. We have a copy in Croatian and in English. Could I ask the usher for his assistance, please. The first document is the decree with the force of law, and the second document is a letter addressed to all the addressees indicated in the letter. This decision, or rather document number 1 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Naumovski until we've got it, make sure the witness has a copy, and also it's given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D4/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) The first document, marked D4/1, is a decree with the force of law on amendments to the decree with the force of law on the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina issued by the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and signed by the president, Alija Izetbegovic, and it was issued on the 6th of August, 1992, and in the Official Gazette of Bosnia-Herzegovina, it was published on the 13th of August, 1992. The second document that we have tendered.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D5/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you. This second document is a letter which the Minister of Defence in the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Jerko Doko, addressed on the 9th of August, 1992, to the general headquarters of the republic or rather the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the general headquarters of the HVO, and so on; I don't think there's any need for me to read out all the addressees.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So Mr. Sahinovic, have you looked at both of these documents, please? Have you seen them before? Are you familiar with them?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have -- I did see this first document before, because we had a rule -- a book of rules of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: This is a little booklet for military use?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but all these details of course are something that I am not very familiar with, as I am not a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, but I just wanted to establish something that is undisputable.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As for the other document, I have not seen it before, this letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So this decision of the presidency is undisputed; you are familiar with it from before?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Having tendered these two documents, could Your Honours allow me to tender a third document which also relates to the same issue, and they comprise a whole?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D6/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you have a copy, Mr. Sahinovic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: This third document is the decision on renaming the formations of the Croatian Defence Council, a decision adopted by the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and signed by the President Alija Izetbegovic, and it was adopted on the 14th of December, 1993, and published in the official gazette of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 31st of December, 1993. It is very brief, Mr. Sahinovic. Have you seen this decision before?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So it is the third document that we wish to tender so as to complete this set of documents. So you didn't have this document in your military book of rules that you referred to a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Finally, a few more questions which are not linked amongst themselves, but I will be very brief. On the 13th of April, 1993, war officers of the HVO were kidnapped by the Mujahedin. This was on the 13th of April, 1993. Do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that they went missing in the direction of Novi Travnik, that is, between the Vodovod and Pecine. And upon my return from Bugojno, when I was coming back from a trip, I was stopped at the HVO checkpoint in Margetici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But I would like you to comment on this kidnapping. How do you know that they went missing? Was their car found?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I just wanted to tell you that I was informed at that checkpoint that three officers and a driver, I think, had disappeared. And I was held there for about half an hour, and personally I asked to get in touch with Skocibusic, who was head of security, so that we could search the area where the officers had gone missing. And they agreed to this at the HVO checkpoint, and they let me go in the direction of Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Were these officers found after the search?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You wanted me to explain the details, and I personally took part in the search, together with a gentleman from the HVO, the search for these missing officers. So if you allow me, let me explain the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't wish us to tire Their Honours with the details. I just asked you whether you knew anything about the negotiations that were conducted about their release. So if you know anything about that, we can talk about it.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know nothing about the negotiations. I just know that together with HVO, I toured Bugojno -- Ravno Rostovo and the barracks where there was a unit of the 7th Muslim Brigade, their warehouses, together with the European Monitors, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Where was this barracks of the 7th Muslim Brigade located?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: One company of about 60 men was located in Ravno Rostovo, I think, and we toured the area together with the European Monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When you're talking about the 7th Muslim Brigade, you're referring to the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm referring to the 7th Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But the Mujahedin were members of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you. The witness said, much earlier, that he knew nothing about Mujahedin, so it really seems rather pointless to go on taking that point. If you want to call evidence about it, of course, you will be able to when it comes to your turn. Is there anything further now for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Perhaps one or two questions. I'm not trying to justify myself, but if the witness hadn't mentioned the 7th Muslim Brigade, I wouldn't have asked about the Mujahedin. So I apologise. If it is your ruling that I shouldn't come back to that issue, I won't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Sahinovic, after the meeting in the factory with Mr. Kordic on the 24th of February, 1992, up until the Washington Agreement, did you ever have any contact with Mr. Kordic again?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: May I correct you? It wasn't in the factory, it was in front of the factory. After that, I had no contact with him, nor did I ever meet with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You never saw him, nor did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Perhaps another question or two, if Your Honours allow me. The villages of Margetici, Pecine, those villages, after June, 1993, were under the control of the BH army, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In view of the fact that I know that these are mostly Croatian settlements, and as far as I know, and at the time I was in the area of Opara, I learned that all the Croatian civilian inhabitants surrendered to the Chetniks in the area of Mravinci Kamenjac and headed off towards Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you learn what the reason for this was? Were these areas attacked by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know, because I was in the area of Opara. But when I came to Novi Travnik, I learned that the Chetniks had reached the lines which had been held by HVO units. And they were already firing at Muslim settlements from those defence lines; that is, the Chetniks were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Will you please answer my question? Did military operations precede the departure of those inhabitants from the villages? I'm referring to military operations by the BH army against these Croatian villages.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that, but I do know that I was there when the BH army was fighting the Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: No, but I'm talking about these villages.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell me, please, are you aware of attacks on the Croatian villages of Sebesic and Rostovo?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In view of the fact that I was working on the prevention of crime in this area, that was my primary task, and an operative group had already been formed, I can't remember exactly how it was called, "G" something, headed by Mehmed Alagic, and, as far as I know, joint forces in this area held the lines towards Sebesic, I couldn't tell you anything about combat operations because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: That wasn't really my question. I didn't want to ask you about combat operations. I wanted to ask you about the destruction of houses and facilities destroyed and damaged in those villages. Do you know anything about that, after June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All I know is that the military police of the security service of Banja Luka, I think, was responsible for the security of the area of Sebesici, and after them, the civilian police of Novi Travnik, so that any destruction after the departure of the Croatian inhabitants is something I'm not aware of, in view of the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you know nothing about the number of houses destroyed, the extent of the damage?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I have no knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I do not wish to tire you any longer. Thank you for your patience. I just wanted to remind you of your permission that after the testimony of this witness, I be granted a few minutes to comment on the videotape shown yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, when the witness has given evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sahinovic, I'm Bozidar Kovacic. I'm a lawyer from Rijeka, and I'm defending Mr. Mario Cerkez. Would you be so kind as to answer some questions? We do not have too many of them, because Mr. Naumovski has already discussed various points with you, and I'm not going to go back to it. But I should like to round off that last part of your discussion, rather the last question about those abandoned villages. You said that Croats had left those villages and surrendered to Serbs and that these tanks had filled that empty space. I'm referring to the area around Sebesic. Was that so?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it was around villages of Margetici and the defence line to Goles, where the Chetniks were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But can that area be entered by tanks; can tanks travel through that area?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You're sure?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Now I should like to ask you about two minor details about what you testified yesterday in chief, just to clarify these points. I believe there were some minor errors in the transcripts. Yesterday, the transcript, page 36, line 7 to 12, it says that you were deputy first responsible for morale, and then it again says "deputy for security." And as far as I remember, you said that in both cases, both times, you were assistant.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You were assistant. So you were an assistant; that was your office? It was not a deputy but assistant?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Assistant commander for morale in the battalion and assistant commander for security at the municipal headquarters in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So I should like to ask that this be rectified. And since we're on that topic, what is the difference between an assistant and a deputy, I mean in the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I am familiar with the military terminology, a deputy commander can be a head, a chief, according to the hierarchy, according to the chain of command in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let me put it in a different way. The highest rank is the commander; is that it?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In the Bosnian language, you say "commander", but I'm referring to the other word in our language. So this is the highest rank, the commander. Who comes next in the normal chain of command?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Head of staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Next?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, the next is assistant commander for morale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And at this level, there are several assistants responsible for individual areas?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Who comes after them?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Let me tell you, there was no legal interpretation. But in our circles, in the circles of that headquarters, we always had debates about who was superior to whom. But assistant commander for security ranked fourth -- fifth, I think, on the hierarchical ladder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Right, so that in the headquarters that you worked in, if I understood properly, it had its own structure, its chain of command. It was headquarters organised along military lines?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And you were obviously ranking rather high on that hierarchical ladder?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If you mean the battalion --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the time when you were responsible for security.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, in the battalion, no, that is not a particularly high-ranking place, but in the command of the municipality headquarters, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Right, thank you. Yesterday, you also said, at the beginning of your testimony in chief, page 39, line 21, as far as I understood your answer, you said that at Bratstvo in Novi Travnik, there were about 70 million dollars worth of stocks, of equipment in stock. Did you say 70 or seven million?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Seventy million dollars.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Seventy million dollars worth of equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So, can this be rectified in the transcript, please? There's 70 million dollars worth of merchandise which Bratstvo was to deliver to the Yugoslav People's Army on the basis of the contract?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Will you please explain that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Bratstvo was to deliver the merchandise manufactured -- made in '91, and there were contracts for those lots. There was a decision of the Bosnian and Herzegovinian government, 6th of '92 -- of the 17th of February that equipment was to be delivered to the Yugoslav People's Army. And the rest, as defined by the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, referring to the future. So the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina was to decide about our production in '92 onward. And the value of stocks covered both these categories.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So this was the stock physically present at the factory, regardless of the legal basis regulating their delivery?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But if I understood this first part of the production, that is, that's made in '91, that was to be delivered to the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think I said it just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you, only. No, no, no, I'm asking you only. Just say "Yes".

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So it was to be delivered to the Yugoslav People's Army, and we're already in '92?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And then you told us that that was why you put up that roadblock and you had those public demonstrations at the crossroads between Novi Travnik and Vitez, because you were concerned about those stocks, since the money was not forthcoming?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The principal reason why we blocked that road and set up the roadblock was that we were asking the Bosnian-Herzegovinian government to take care of the workers socially, to give us either some food or give us some kind of money. All we wanted was that the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina take care of the social status of workers, since they had manufactured, produced, something, and had not been paid for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, right, but let's leave that aside. One of your arguments that was comprised of that bulletin that you gave us, you said, "This is merchandise. We've got money, because merchandise is money, so relieve us of this merchandise. Rather give us some means of livelihood." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Right, yes, let's leave it. Let's not go into it. I think we do understand one another. At the same time, did you know that in Croatia, the aggression had already begun, I mean the Yugoslav People's Army supported by local Serbs against Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you at that time have a television, did Sarajevo Television still operate normally?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And you could see in the news that war was raging in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And that JNA was an aggressor; did you already understand that, did you understand the JNA was an aggressor in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you understand that there was an international embargo on the delivery of weapons to the parties to the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you could see that there was war in Croatia, that people were being killed?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go back to your role in the army of B and A, when you became an officer. Will you please, just to see if we know what we are talking about, a battalion in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, ideally speaking, how strong it should be, how many men it should have? Just tell me how strong should it be? How many men is the ideal size of a battalion, and how many men should be in the command of such a battalion?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I would not know the -- I would not know exactly. All I know is that in that battalion, we never had more than 80 per cent of all the men due to that formation, and that is, I think, not more than 208, as far as I can remember, at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So at the time when it was only 80 per cent strong, I mean that battalion in terms of an ideal battalion, how many men were in the command of that battalion?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the battalion, I think seven or eight -- seven or eight, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. And the brigade, how strong should a brigade of the BH army be, roughly?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know. I must apologise here. I'm not familiar with that terminology, since I did not even serve in that army then, so I'm really not conversant with the terminology of those units. And believe me, I really do not know how many men there should be in a brigade, but I'm quite sure that it was not -- never 100 per cent strong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But the one that you belonged to, 308th, how many battalions did it have at its peak, shall we say, in late '93?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In late '93, it had three battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So, if every battalion had about 250, so altogether it should be, shall we say, if we round it up, about 800 men?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Please, when you spoke about your movements and your biography, we heard that you were the leader in Bratstvo, you were the union leader in Bratstvo, and I assume that you are familiar with that company because you worked there for a long time. Could you please tell us something else? And let me try to expedite matters, and just answer with "Yes" or "No". Bratstvo is only one link in the chain of the military industry in Bosnia at the time?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Shall we take your product which you mentioned yesterday, say, Oganj. As a layman, I understand that Oganj is a device which launches projectiles?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's a rocket system.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: It is used to launch projectiles; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So Bratstvo made those launching systems; "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It made the mechanical part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Wait, wait a moment. So, it made the mechanical part of the system and the projectiles?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, Bratstvo did not make them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And who did make the projectiles?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If I remember well, it was Pretis Vogosca in Sarajevo, but Bratstvo never made any projectiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But since you worked for the military industry, and we're talking about that, a projectile is -- and I'm a layman, it has an iron part, that is, the sleeve and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And the rocket motor and the rocket engine, so it has an iron part, it has a drive, and that drive needs fuel to be driven, and explosive -- I don't know what it's called, really.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And who then made this rocket fuel; do you know?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And who made the explosive?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, explosive was made in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So if somebody wishes to control the military industry in Bosnia, he needs at least three factories to make one whole piece?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Until 1992, we made those systems, but as of '92, Bratstvo company could not make a single piece.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Because it lacked the components, the optical part of it and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So, for this kind of manufacturing, for this kind of production to go on, and somebody who wishes to control that kind of production, he needs to have several plants under his control?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Bratstvo was held throughout the conflict between the Muslims and the Croats in '93, Bratstvo was, by in large, held by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Orkan and Vitezit in Banja Luka, who was in control --

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I mean electronics that was needed for lasers, for Orkan, the electronics for Orkan -- I don't know where that was made -- it was not under your control?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: It wasn't?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And Vitezit, in Vitez, was it under the control of the army of B and H?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean Vitez, the plant?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let us move on. At some point in time, you said that you attended a meeting where again the question of those stocks in the plant was being discussed and that, among other people, Vinko Pavelic was present. He also said that he was lieutenant colonel of the JNA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Was he the manager of the production or sales?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Production, or rather he was the manager of the factory, excuse me. Excuse me, I do apologise. He was the manager of the plant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So, Vinko Pavelic, I'm referring to early '92, February and early March, '93 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Vinko Pavelic was the plant manager, he was a JNA lieutenant colonel, and that is a military factory, and we have the war in Croatia and you insisted on the delivery of these weapons into Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. If you understand us, we never insisted on the delivery to the Yugoslav People's Army, we never insisted on delivering the armaments to the Yugoslav People's Army. What we were asking for was to resolve the social status of workers, and we were asking the management also, and the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina to solve the social status.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Apart from that part of the obligations contracted in '91?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When you joined the Territorial Defence, which then became the army of B and H, who was the enemy?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I joined the Territorial Defence and offered my services to the Territorial Defence, only the Chetniks were our enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And who were the Chetniks? Will you please tell the Court? Perhaps the Court is not familiar with our folklore.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, to be quite clear, all those who fired at us and sided with the Yugoslav People's Army. We perceived them all as Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So it was the Yugoslav People's Army supported by local Serbs? Can we say that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Armed local Serbs. So the Serb side were the JNA and local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And that was only four or five months before this delivery of weapons?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, all right. If the Court permits -- no, let me ask you another question. At that time, before the conflict with Croats, I mean in '92 -- in '92 for the most part, that is until October '92 -- the line against the Chetniks, against the JNA, did you share it with Croats, with the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Above Turbe, there were no Croat forces facing the Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but they were behind our backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let me simplify the question. Did the Territorial Defence, in 1992, was it fighting against the Serbs in the area of your municipality, rather, in the boundary areas? They held the line at Kamenjac, you held this line, you had your troops there, and you were on that front with Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but we had one and they had another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No, but Serbs are your enemy. I'm talking about the TO. Did the HVO also hold some sectors? Were they doing the same thing?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So both the TO and the HVO held the front against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: At that time?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) With the Court's leave, I should like to show a document to the witness. We have a sufficient number of copies, but unfortunately we did not succeed with the -- have not translated it because we only yesterday realised that it could be interesting for this witness, but we can of course order translation immediately. It is a very short document, and we shall give it to the interpreters so that they can read it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, the rule is that the documents are translated before they are admitted into evidence, and it's only in exceptional circumstances that we will allow documents in an untranslated state to be put in; but since this is the first occasion, we will allow you to do so, and because it's short, but on the whole, the documents must be translated before they can be put into evidence. It may be that this document can be interpreted. Is there a copy for the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Yes, we do have a copy for interpreters, and we apologise once again. We simply realised it would be good to adduce this now. We have some more documents, and some of them were translated, but I believe we have another one which has not been translated yet. So if we can ask, then, the usher to take those documents. Your Honours, perhaps it would be best if we asked the interpreters to read this document aloud.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This copy is illegible. Mr. Kovacic, we are not going to let you put this document in. It's not legible. It's not translated. Once it's translated and done properly, then you can put it in. Meanwhile, we'll hand it back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sahinovic, leave the document; we'll not do it now. But you did mention Mr. Malbasic as commander of Stjepan Tomasevic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In view of your office, you evidently met him on various occasions, heard from him?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I met him during the negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you ever attend some concrete negotiations or talks with Stjepan Tomasevic representatives in relation to that front above Turbe which you held against the Serbs, regarding the deployment of units, shifts, passage of troops through places, any matter concerning inevitable cooperation on the front?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time I was not the assistant commander for security in the brigade, so that I did not take part in negotiations or talks or preparations for joint actions in that capacity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But have you heard of such talks and agreements?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were no talks until Mr. Boro Malbasic came. When Mr. Boro Malbasic arrived, the first negotiations and talks took place, and I think, since I was there, I think this commander was the man who I could cooperate with, talk about and expect that -- what the agreed things would be complied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So this was the cooperation between these troops and the HVO while Mr. Malbasic was commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We did not have those agreements as regards Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I don't understand you. Will you please tell us, can we conclude from what you are saying that there was cooperation between the HVO and the TO, or rather the Armija, regarding defence against the Serbs while Malbasic was the commander?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You've just told us there was.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were talks and cooperation in the area of Novi Travnik, trying to bring down the tension caused by the arrival of Herzegovinians and so forth. That is what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You just mentioned Herzegovinians, and you mentioned them yesterday. Just one sentence, will you please confirm it: You say there was unrest in the town when the Herzegovinians came?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether HVO did something to put those Herzegovinians under control? Have you ever heard anything about it in view of what you did?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I heard it from Mr. Boro Malbasic, during the negotiations of the 13th, that I had invited the Bruno Busic unit to put things in Novi Travnik in order, because they could not keep things under control. That is what he said, that was his explanation, during the negotiations in January.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Was the impression that you gained then that the commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was trying to put the problem under control?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When Mr. Boro Malbasic arrived, yes, it was my impression that he was really trying to put things in order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you ever heard of an incident which happened at that time, and I will tell you that it was on the 10th of February in Novi Travnik, in Kodadjura, a coffee bar, Duro Matinovic was the owner, when Zoran Jukic, an HVO soldier, was killed, when the HVO police intervened. Have you heard anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I knew this young man, because he was my neighbour when I lived in that part of the town, and I heard that he had been killed, but I do not know the circumstances of his death.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honour, I apologise, but yesterday we found this document. It is a very short document -- it is a note, rather, a communication for the public -- and we have it both translated into English and -- we can hand it over to you, and we can ask the witness to read it and then see whether this is what we are talking about. Will you please help us?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D1/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Just to explain to Your Honours and the Prosecution, it was D218 in the Blaskic case. It was already tendered in the Blaskic case. You can see the number up there already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you have time to read it, or do you need more time?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: This public announcement that you have just read, does it relate to that event that I asked you a while ago? Has it reminded you of that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is true that at that time, it culminated at that time; but the circumstances in which this soldier died, I knew nothing about then, until I read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But what did you hear about that event at that time? You said you had heard that he had been killed, and you knew him, and you did not hear anything else?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You only heard that he had been killed?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You did not hear what happened on that occasion, how it came about?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: This does not remind you of that story, of that rumour which was spread around the town then?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, because information did not reach us easily at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But could you infer from this that it has to do with the death of the late Jukic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't understand. I don't understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Now that you've read this announcement, now that you have read it, do you think that it is related to that event when you heard that Jukic had been killed at the time when you heard about it?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, it's now 11:15. Are you going to be very much longer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I'm not really sure. I think I'll need about 20 minutes more, but this is a convenient time for us to make a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have another witness here, I take it, Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I hope, if we put on as much speed as possible, we can finish that witness tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That may be optimistic. We'll have to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I should like to make a correction in the transcript. It should have said the people of Herzegovina, Herzegovci, the Herzegovinians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sahinovic, we were mentioning the Herzegovinians. Will you tell us, please, Herzegovina, is that a province within the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is it a geographic part of the State of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So these Herzegovinians that we were talking about, they come from the same State, don't they?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned the Vitezovi, a unit of some 25 men that were captured.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: This group that you were in touch with personally, did they have their own insignia?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not personally in touch with that group, but in the service that I was working in, I learned that the group was from Vitez and that they were Vitezovi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you have only indirect knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, from my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that they had their own insignia?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear what those insignia looked like? What was written on them?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They wore the HOS insignia -- no, I'm sorry, I apologise: Not HOS. No, no, no, but they had the insignia of Vitezovi. That was a slip of the tongue; I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But in any way, you do know that they originate from the HOS?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But in any event, they wore insignia which indicated their membership of a unit?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did they have any recognizable kind of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, they wore regular camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said yesterday that you didn't know who their commander was?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You are referring to the unit that was captured, or generally, the commander of the Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Generally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Does the name "Darko Kraljevic" mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Darko Kraljevic? I've heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Could you link that name with the Vitezovi, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, you told us that you had two direct encounters with the accused, Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So I should like to ask you a few questions about that first encounter, the negotiations on the 13th of January.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You said something to the effect that this was a meeting attended by representatives of both armies and parties -- that is, the SDA and the HDZ -- and it was devoted to a settlement of the situation and crime control in town; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The meeting was convened, and I was precise about this, because of the new development with the arrival of the Herzegovinians in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But the reason was to ease tensions and restore peace?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In connection with that meeting, did you, as a unit of the BH army, receive any order or any kind of instructions or any kind of document at all from the commander of the Bosnian army, Mr. Sefer Halilovic, instructions regarding the need to engage in negotiations to ease tensions?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you're not aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SAHINOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, if I may, I should like to tender a document. We have a translation and a sufficient number of copies for Your Honours, and then I should like to ask the witness a couple of questions regarding that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) May I ask the usher for his assistance, please.
