And this astounded me, knowing Mr. Pero Kordic, when at a certain point in time at a luncheon in the church prepared by the parish priest of the Franciscan Church, St. Ante, and he asked Mr. Boras to try, in the HDZ, to do something for his son, Dario, in the sense of promotion in the hierarchy. And he also appealed to Mr. Boras with the same request. Mr. Boras at the time didn't know Mr. Dario Kordic, but he was a good friend of his father's, Dr. Pero, Pero Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So far as you're aware, did Mr. Boris respond to that request or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: I doubt that Mr. Boris could do anything, because, anyway, it was not necessary for him to do anything for Mr. Dario Kordic, since at the time Mr. Boban appeared on the scene. And after that, it was not necessary for anyone to do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Because?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Because the influence of Mr. Boban by far exceeded that of Mr. Boris. And Mr. Boris was gradually disappearing from the political stage, whereas climbing on that stage with full force was Mr. Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What was the next development of Dario Kordic in the party? What was the next thing that happened locally? Did he achieve office, or what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: The HDZ of Busovaca never had an office for the president, and Mr. Dario Kordic used the office of the Secretariat of National Defence in the municipality, therefore within the state administration of Busovaca, and he became president of the HDZ of the Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How did that come about, that he became president?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Mr. Boras, at the elections, became a member of parliament, and it was not possible for him, at the same time, to be a member of parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina and at the same time to be president of the municipality board of the HDZ of Busovaca. And then Mr. Kordic was proposed to take over that duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Do you remember by whom he was proposed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you support it, oppose it, were you neutral, or can't you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: I supported it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And at that time, was the defendant associated with any group of other people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic always had a certain animosity towards all people coming outside of Busovaca, and this applied to me as well, as his deputy president. And he had this animosity towards me, as he did towards Dr. Boras and others, because we had come from the town of Zenica. Mr. Kordic, together with his associates, though he was not born in Busovaca, but he considered himself to be a native, whereas these other people were born in Busovaca, so he considered them to have much greater priority than those of us who had come from elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Who were in this group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: The main support for him was always Mr. Anto Sliskovic, his brother, Mr. Franjo Sliskovic, then Mr. Igor Prusac, Mr. Anto Stipic, Mr. Florijan Glavocevic and the others. I don't know if it's necessary for me to enumerate them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What sort of people were these, what sort of jobs did they do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Various jobs, but they were of medium skills --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Let the interpreter find the proper term for this. "Secondary school education."

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: -- except for Florijan Glavocevic, who was a forester. In our country, these are usually administrative clerks who have these secondary skills or secondary school qualifications.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did Dario Kordic enjoy any security by reason of this group of people or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: He was the absolute master of these people. These men protected him. But whatever he said, they carried out without any question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was there any training in respect of these men, or any of them, that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: I don't know in what sense you mean "training." Civilian or military?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Military.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Military training. I see. When the danger threatened over Yugoslavia, when Slovenia and Croatia had been attacked without any reason, a shock group was formed in Busovaca, headed by Anto and Franjo Sliskovic. This was a group that trained using weapons that were smuggled into Bosnia and Busovaca illegally. This training ground was in the mountains near Busovaca. They trained with the most sophisticated weapons, which they had never in their lives come across, and I believe that was the first time they saw them. And this was one part of the training that they had in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was there any other part of training that you can help us with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: I could just say, actually, a part of training that does not apply to Busovaca alone. In Herzegovina, there was a military unit of the HOS, headed by Blaz Kraljevic. This was a highly-sophisticated unit, very well organised, and then all the municipal HDZ organisations that wanted to have professionally-trained military men would send some of their young men to be trained there by Mr. Blaz Kraljevic. In addition, they would be given a golden badge, showing that they had been trained in his training centre in Herzegovina. I'm not quite sure where it was situated, but I think it was somewhere around Capljina, so that young men from Busovaca went to that centre there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Those men who provided security for Kordic, did they wear any distinctive clothing at any stage or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: If they were performing ordinary civil duties, then they did not wear any particular markings. But if they were out on an action or where Mr. Kordic would send them, then they would be wearing the then military clothes, today they are called camouflage uniforms, with modern weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Once he had been appointed within the party, did you meet him from time to time or regularly? What was the position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Once Kordic had become a member of the party and, indeed, an officer of the party, he being a person you had never known before, did you now meet him regularly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: We established contact very quickly, and there was no need for it, because we met quite often, very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he express any views as to where the HDZ should be going; for example, any views about the approach coming from Tudjman, in Zagreb, or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: We talked about that very often, and his view was that one should side with the HDZ of the Republic of Croatia, that we should be part of the movement promoted by Mr. Tudjman; that is, all Croats in the HDZ, wherever they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you agree with that view?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: No, I did not, because I always thought Bosnia-Herzegovina should stay between the Una, the Drina, the Sava, and the sea and that we should have an independent HDZ organisation. And either Mr. Kordic, or Mr. Kljuic, or any other gentleman could be in the lead of that organisation, but it should be an independent HDZ organisation of the Bosnia-Herzegovina and in no way become a part of the HDZ of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you make your position clear to Kordic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: One other man I want your help with at the moment; Kostroman. Tell us about him, please. Did you know him before the HDZ or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: I don't remember if I knew him before. It is a man who even when you meet him, you don't remember him for long. But during the HDZ, I did, indeed, come to know him very well. Should I go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What views did he hold?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Quite opposite. To this day, when I start to think about that, I cannot understand what were his views and what did he want, really, with the HDZ and B and H, because it was the first time in history that a technical secretary, that is, an administrative secretary, not the Secretary-General, that such secretary works against his party and its president, and the president was Mr. Kljuic. And he completely turned about and worked with Mr. Boban, who absolutely had no right to work with Mr. Kostroman. So Kostroman is what people would say is a person without a personality, who has inflicted a great deal on the Croat people in Bosnia-Herzegovina and, I believe, also of the Croat people in the Republic of Croatia as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So to summarise, you, in your locality, and Kljuic outside, favoured a multi-ethnic Bosnia-Herzegovina, but --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- Dario Kordic, Mate Boban, who had connections to Zagreb, favoured a different conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In summary, we'll look at documents a little later, how did things unfold, and can you now perhaps give the Court some dates or some approximate dates? If you can summarise the position, and then we'll look at the documents later.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Unfolding of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. How did events unfold? What, for example, ultimately happened to Mr. Kljuic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Mr. Kostroman was -- wait now. Now, of course, you -- well, you have to know some things. No, no. The main office of Mr. Kljuic and Secretary-General Mr. Markesic was separated --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We can come back to this if it's necessary, but in summary, what happened to Mr. Kljuic? Did he stay in office or did he lose office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: No, Mr. Kljuic was eliminated gradually from the office of the president of HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: To be replaced by --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: By the professor -- Dr. Miljenko Brkic came to succeed him, and I don't really know how he turned up in that group. And after him was Mr. Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: At the local party, and we're going to deal with the detail of this later, but at the local party, were you able to stay a member of the party, holding the views you did, or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: With great difficulty, with great difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Give me a minute, please. Your Honour, I think it might be convenient now to get the witness to deal with some documents which will, I think, help the Court. These documents were all in the core bundle, and indeed many of them were referred to in the opening. I've got them all fresh for the Court now. I don't know what the Court wants to do with its core bundle, but it's probably better if I provide, certainly at this stage, exhibits full and fresh, and the Court can make its own decisions in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: But I'll read out the pages, in case any of my learned friends are following in the way that the Registry ordered documents. So we'll go first, please, to Z7, Registry page 5818, and if this can be provided to the Court and, in its BCS version, to the witness. If the usher could stay by the ELMO, detaching the English version from the BSC version in order to display the paragraphs, and there won't be very many of them, for a document that I'll ask the witness to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Cicak, what we have here is a document headed "The HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Travnik Region," dated the 21st of July, page 1 being an agenda. Before we turn from the agenda, we can see that it says its for the leaders of all seven municipalities of the Travnik region. It sets out those regions, and it sets out a list of people attending, which does not include you. So the first point is this: Did you attend meetings of the leaders of the municipalities of the Travnik region or not, or was it sometimes? Help us, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: I did attend most of the meetings. But I must explain one thing to the Court, that these original agendas which were typewritten, they are not the original agendas, they are copies, they are transcripts, but I don't know of what, because this is Mr. Kostroman, at his own discretion, adopted and wrote texts, so that not one text was adopted ever at any one meeting of the HDZ. It could have been discussed in different ways, but Mr. Kostroman, in his office, would reword it to his liking, and such documents were never adopted. What I'm trying to say is that we do not have handwritten minutes, and these minutes are not signed, even, apart from Kostroman, who wrote them, so that --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Do you know, one way or another, whether you definitely attended the meeting on the 21st --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: I think I was present at that meeting. I know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We now turn to the second sheet in the English version. There is something headed "Conclusions," of which paragraph 4 in the English reads: "HDZ BiH president, Stjepan Kljuic, is ordered to call an urgent session of the HDZ BiH main board on Wednesday, the 24th of July, 1991, because of the new situation. It is necessary to invite the leaders of the HDZ from Zagreb to attend the session." First, do you recall any meeting where such a decision, that is, the decision to call the president of the party to -- sorry, where the decision is expressed to be an instruction to the party's president to call a session of the main board, do you recall being present at any meeting where that decision was made?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Yes. We asked Mr. Kljuic to attend our meetings on various occasions, on various occasions, but this is nonsense, because a regional community can never order the president or the presidency of the HDZ to do something. That is, somebody who is inferior cannot order his superior to do something. That is sheer nonsense, and we never had conclusions worded as that. It is quite possibly that Mr. Kljuic was criticised at the time and told that he should more frequently attend regional committees and more frequently talk about the situation. But it could never happen, nor could one ever write or even say in the discussion that Mr. President Stjepan Kljuic is ordered to do this or that. I mean it simply did not happen. So this is pure --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Would you now please turn to conclusion number 6, which is a rather longer paragraph and reads: "The Croatia Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina must take a clear position with regard to the latest political events, namely, aggression against Slovenia, Croatia, and the silent occupation of parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina; the Federal Presidency's decision to withdraw the troops of the so-called JNA from Slovenia and their deployment in Bosnia-Herzegovina and other parts of the rump Yugoslavia; the status of Bosnia-Herzegovina; the relations with other parties; a clear stand if the SDA decides to remain within the rump Yugoslavia or, rather, Serboslavia; about the statement made by the BiH Presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, that he requires the representatives of Bosnia-Herzegovina to attend a conference of Islamic countries, even without previous consent of the Presidency; and other topical issues." I read the whole text, but I really want your comment on the last passage about Alija Izetbegovic. Do you recall anything being said about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What was said?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Well, precisely as this said. Perhaps it was more expanded. Mr. Izetbegovic embraced the practice, and I believe he does it to this day, that all that he does or all decisions that he takes, he does so personally. He never consults a wider circle of people, one man perhaps and nobody else, and this was one such instance. But again, it is nonsense that Croat representatives, members of the presidency, do not bring any pressure to bear on Mr. Izetbegovic to change those decisions regarding the so-called rump Yugoslavia or attendance at a conference of Islamic countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Then, as you've already explained, in the original version that you hold, it's typed, and over the typed name of "Kostroman," there is some initials or signature, but over the name of "Dario Kordic," "Chairman," or -- in fact, perhaps I would ask you to read out the title under Dario Kordic's name and then the interpreters can tell us what it is. What's the title under Dario Kordic's name? Is that "President"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: No, no, it is "Chairman," chairman of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: But there is, on the version you have, no signature over that name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: No. Well, this is Kostroman's -- this was written by Mr. Kostroman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next exhibit, please, is Z8. Registry page number 5814 in the BCS original and English. Thank you. May the witness have the -- is this a document headed "The Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina? It's dated the 30th of July, 1991 --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- for a meeting in Vitez, with an agenda set out. And again does your name not appear in the list of those attending?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: No. I did not attend that meeting. It was attended by the leaders of the municipal boards of the HDZ, and Mr. Anto Valenta chaired the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you tell us something, please, about Anto Valenta? What was his role, what was his position on political matters? Again, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Very briefly, he was a great supporter of the foundation of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. In body and spirit, he dedicated himself to the realisation of that idea. By occupation he's a teacher. He wrote a book, which I consider to be stupid, entitled "Humane Resettlement." Any kind of resettlement cannot be humane, but he wrote such a book, entitled "Humane Resettlement," meaning that in Bosnia-Herzegovina, where there are minority groups and there are majorities in another area, they should be unified, and the same should apply to all three ethnic groups: That is, the Muslims, Serbs, and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He wrote such a book. What views did he espouse in meetings or any other political activities at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: At first he was a moderate, a moderate member of the HDZ. Just before the war, or rather before the outbreak of the conflict between the Bosniaks and the Muslims, he was very extreme, and when I met him since, I felt as if he was not a living person any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he express any views on the possibility of Muslims and Croats living together in the same territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Would you turn, please, to the second sheet of the original, as we turn to the second sheet of the English version, and at the foot of the English page -- I'm sorry, I think it's probably the top of the third sheet in the original -- does this appear: "Because of its geographic position and because it is a centre of the district, municipal HDZ board in Busovaca is appointed headquarters of the Travnik regional community. Dario Kordic is appointed coordinator of the regional community and in the future will call and chair the meetings." Was that decision made?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were you aware in advance that it was being considered and made, or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: I didn't know in advance that such a decision was being considered, but all of us in Busovaca were surprised by that decision, which shows that Mr. Kordic, outside the municipal board of the HDZ, was climbing very quickly in the hierarchy of the HDZ. It is inconceivable that a former president who headed the regional community of Travnik, that is Professor Martin Udovicic, should leave the leadership of the regional community and its movement to Busovaca. After all, it's called the Travnik regional community, and it is being moved 20 or 30 kilometres southwards to the village of Busovaca. Furthermore, it wasn't clear to us how Mr. Kordic could have so quickly climbed to the position of coordinator of all the communities in the region. So this is indicative of another trend in Mr. Kordic's career.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Staying with this document, going back up the document to the beginning of Item 3, was this set out as one of the conclusions? "Support is given to the HDZ initiative to set up a new Croatian Government which is to consist of Croatian experts regardless of their political orientation if their beliefs are not in opposition with the common interests of the Croatian people." Were you aware of that decision?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Yes, very well aware of it, and it was widespread and very popular among the public, it being said that this would be something very positive. However, I was absolutely against it, because it meant the complete division of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the inability for it to function in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, because if each community had its own governments and its own logistics, then all the bodies of Bosnia-Herzegovina would be paralysed. So this idea on the formation of a Croatian government was in existence among HDZ members, but I think that it never found supporters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, we'll go on till 10 past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We know you weren't present at this particular meeting, but that you were present at another, and we're going to see others. Your opposition to these ideas, did you express your opposition when you had an opportunity do so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: All the ideas that were not close to mine, I clearly expressed my disagreement with such ideas. Whether people like that or not, I don't know, but always, at all meetings, I said loud and clear that I did not agree with certain ideas leading towards the division of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the formation of ethnic ghettos, et cetera, et cetera. As Mr. Kordic said on one occasion, I was opposed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what was that --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: You keep interrupting me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Mr. Kordic said what? If you could just complete that answer: As Mr. Kordic said on one occasion ... ?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Wrote what he said on many occasions, but in a rather charming article entitled "The Small Judas" --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We're going to come to that later, and I'll deal with it in its correct position.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Probably I've shrunk, so I look like a little Judas now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: But the question I want you to deal with at this stage is this: You've had an opportunity to look at -- and we're going to take the Court through several -- you've had an opportunity to look through a number of minutes of meetings. Is there ever, in the minutes you've been able to read, a setting-out of your views which were contrary to the views of the defendant Kordic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Never. Views that were contrary to the policy of the HDZ were never entered in the minutes. Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Next exhibit, then, please, is 11, registry page 5811, the first page of which shows this is from the -- or of the Croatian Democratic Community of Bosnia and Herzegovina, dated the 13th of August of 1991, reflecting a third session held in Busovaca on the 13th of August, same day. In this document, under "Agenda," you are shown as present, beside "Busovaca" and immediately after the name "Dario Kordic." And we see, if we turn over to the second sheet, and of the English version, about five lines down, that the session was also attended by Mr. Mate Boban, vice-president of HDZ-BiH, and sets out what the other officers were -- who the other officers were and what they did. Can we go straight, please, to paragraph 3 of the decisions, which reads in English as follows: "The behaviour of Stjepan Kljuic, president of the HDZ BiH, while conducting the session of the HDZ BiH main board on 6 August 1991, is judged as unbefitting and unacceptable. He skilfully managed to avert discussion on the Decisions at the Travnik Regional Community, although his attention was several times directed to the material on hand and the agenda adopted." That's set out as a conclusion. Do you remember that matter being raised and discussed, or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: It was a customary issue, because Mr. Kljuic, due to his other engagements in the state presidency, did not appear in the field, or rather did very rarely. However, this is a document that shows how the position of the president of a party is being undermined, in this case, Mr. Kljuic, as the president of the HDZ of BiH. No regional communities, no meetings in Busovaca, Travnik, or anywhere else, could give orders or assess the behaviour of a party president, the president of a legal party in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Only his assembly may do that, his presidency, his secretariat, and other such bodies. No one has the right to interfere in the affairs of the president, Mr. Kljuic, and this was nonsense that was repeated time and time again, but which tells us that Mr. Kordic and Mr. Kostroman and Mr. Boban were persistently working on the separation of Mr. Kljuic from his main base, his supporters in HDZ, for them to take over and to leave Kljuic in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'll interrupt you there, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: You keep interrupting me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, I don't want to interrupt my opposition's smooth flow of cross-examination, but that political diatribe was absolutely nonresponsive to the question asked. He proceeded to elaborate into an expression of his own political views, and I think that, with all due respect, the witness should be asked to answer the question a little bit more succinctly and directly without giving vent to his own political views. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I don't agree with that analysis, necessarily. It seems to me the witness was asked an opinion about a political matter, and inevitably he is going to answer in a political way. But perhaps, Mr. Nice, you could get to the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's a question of judging when to jump in and cut off. It's not that easy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: But I want to take you, please, Mr. Cicak, to another sheet which is part of the same exhibit, which we have in the English starting at the second -- I'm sorry, I beg your pardon, the third sheet in English -- and it's a letter of the same date, the 13th of August, 1991, and then it goes over, I think, to subparagraph 7. It's a slightly confusing exhibit, but nevertheless it's part of what appears to be a letter of the same date. It begins -- do you have paragraph 7, Mr. Cicak? Something that begins with letters "d," "e," "f," "g," "h," "i," and then goes "5," "6," and "7"? Do you find that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And does paragraph 7 read --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- "The Regional Community boards are instructed -- and other boards are encouraged -- to make contact with Mate BOBAN in order to familiarise themselves with the superior level of organisation in certain Herzegovinian municipality boards and to exchange useful information in the new situation." Was this the first time that Mr. Boban had appeared at a meeting in Busovaca, or had he been at earlier meetings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Mr. Boban did not appear this time for the first time. He had appeared several times. This is an accurate reading of the conclusion adopted. Since I am not allowed to speak politically, I will answer your questions as you've put them to me. This is Number 7, yes, and that is what is stated there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you remember whose proposal it was, or if more than one person, which number of people's proposal it was, that there should be contact with Mate Boban for these purposes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: I don't know, but I think it was Mr. Martin Udovicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Then finally, going back up the document --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, if my memory is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. Going back up the document to the first of the decisions, Number 1 on the decisions, on the second sheet in English, decision number 1 reads: "The Travnik Regional Community of the HDZ BiH continues to uphold its decisions of 21 and 30 July 1991 and requests each member of the Presidency of the HDZ BiH to state his or her attitude toward each of the said Decisions as well as toward each of the Decisions reached at today's session." First, were you a member of the relevant presidency concerned -- that is, the presidency of the HDZ BiH -- or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: I was never a member of the presidency of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina, because that is the highest level in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, was this decision made and formulated --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Something must be wrong here. I can't find the text, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Sorry. Decision number 1, and it's probably on the last sheet.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: I see. That's something quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If you can't find it and if the usher hands me the papers, I'll find it for you. Have you found it? I'll read it again and see if you agree with the translation: "The Travnik Regional Community of the HDZ BiH continues to uphold its decisions of 21 and 30 July and requests each member of the Presidency of the HDZ BiH to state his or her attitude toward each of the said Decisions as well as toward each of the Decisions reached at today's session." Now, was that discussed at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: Not in this way. May I comment? May I be allowed, Your Honours, to say a few words?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: It is impossible, I repeat again, for a small community of a small town to request from Sarajevo that members of the presidency should express their positions. That is just impossible, absolutely impossible, and that was not discussed. What we did discuss was that members of the presidency need to take a stand as to how they would behave in the future in Bosnia-Herzegovina, but it is not possible to demand from a member of the presidency of the HDZ of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: That is my first point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He has a second point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, if you could tell us it quickly, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN ZVONIMIR CICAK
utterances.text: If the members of the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina don't do that, and they come from all over Bosnia-Herzegovina, if they fail to do that -- that is, to express their personal views on the events -- that will be interpreted as being tendentious, and that is again nonsense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, is that a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. The next exhibit is a short one, but it can be taken tomorrow morning as easily as this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: How much more do you have in chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Producing the exhibits -- which once done, of course, is done for good -- is likely to take at least another 40 minutes, and then there's evidence of fact. So it's at least half the morning and possibly most of the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Cicak, would you be back, please, tomorrow morning at 9.45. Could you remember, please, not to speak to anybody about your evidence while you're giving it, and that includes speaking to members of the Office of the Prosecutor about it. Thank you very much. 9.45, then, tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I reply? May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There's no need.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you for making it at 9.45. Otherwise it's too early for me to get up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: 4:10 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 23rd day of April, 1999, at 9.45 a.m.
